---
title: "Fifteen tests, four sports: the example data"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 4.6, dpi = 110, out.width = "100%")
library(lactater)
plex <- requireNamespace("systemfonts", quietly = TRUE) &&
  isTRUE(suppressMessages(systemfonts::require_font("IBM Plex Sans", fallback = "sans")))
if (plex) options(lactater.font = "IBM Plex Sans")
```

`lactate_tests` holds 15 incremental step tests, one row per stage, so you can try every part of lactater on data
that looks like what you will collect. Twelve are real tests from two open datasets (Trinity College Dublin, and
[Heuberger et al., 2018](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0206846); both CC BY 4.0); three are simulated where no open data exists. This article walks through
them: what each sport looks like, and the cases that need care.

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(lactater)
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

lactate_tests |>
  distinct(sport, test, description, source) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "sport") |>
  cols_label(test = "Test", description = "Description", source = "Source") |>
  tab_style(cell_text(font = "IBM Plex Mono", size = px(13)), cells_body(columns = test)) |>
  gt_lactater() |>
  tab_options(row_group.text_transform = "capitalize")
```

A small helper analyses one test, with heart rate and RPE when they were recorded (the RPE of the three simulated
tests is simulated too):

```{r}
analyse <- function(name, ...) {
  one <- lactate_tests |>
    filter(test == name)
  hr <- if (!anyNA(one$heart_rate)) "heart_rate"
  rating <- if (!anyNA(one$rpe)) "rpe"
  one |>
    lactate_threshold(
      intensity, lactate, heart_rate_column = hr, rpe_column = rating, sport = first(one$sport), plot = FALSE, ...
    )
}
```

## How far apart do the methods land?

Every method answers a slightly different question, so on the same test they land at different intensities. Here,
for each test, the lowest and highest threshold as a percentage of the highest intensity of the test:

```{r}
spread <- lactate_tests |>
  distinct(test, sport) |>
  mutate(thresholds = purrr::map(test, \(name) {
    analyse(name, ltp_breakpoints = if (name == "submaximal") 1 else 2) |>
      relative_thresholds() |>
      select(method, percent_peak)
  })) |>
  tidyr::unnest(thresholds) |>
  summarise(
    thresholds = sum(!is.na(percent_peak)),
    lowest = round(min(percent_peak, na.rm = TRUE)),
    highest = round(max(percent_peak, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .by = c(test, sport)
  )
spread
```

In every test the thresholds span a wide part of the intensity range, from the first rise of lactate to the methods
aimed at the maximal lactate steady state. That is why a threshold means little without the name of its method,
and why [Training zones](zones.html) asks you to choose LT1 and LT2.

## Cycling: an elite and a trained rider

Power in watts, 3-min stages. The elite rider reached 440 W, 6.6 W/kg; the trained female rider 300 W, 5.0 W/kg.
Same methods, very different curves.

```{r, fig.height = 8}
elite <- analyse("cycling_elite")
autoplot(elite)
```

Per kg of body mass, and as a percentage of the highest power, the two riders can be compared:

```{r}
female <- analyse("cycling_female")
body_mass <- function(name) {
  lactate_tests |>
    filter(test == name) |>
    pull(body_mass) |>
    first()
}

bind_rows(
  cycling_elite = relative_thresholds(elite, body_mass("cycling_elite")),
  cycling_female = relative_thresholds(female, body_mass("cycling_female")),
  .id = "rider"
) |>
  filter(method %in% c("LTP1", "LTP2")) |>
  select(rider, method, intensity, intensity_per_kg, percent_peak)
```

## Running: speed and pace

Treadmill speed in km/h at 0% grade. lactater adds the pace (s/km) and shows it as minutes per km in the plots.

```{r}
running <- analyse("running")
running |>
  filter(method %in% c("Log-log", "OBLA 4.0", "LTP2")) |>
  select(method, intensity, pace, lactate, heart_rate)
autoplot(running, "LTP2")
```

## Rowing: power and the 500 m split

Ergometer power in watts, with 1 min of rest between 3-min stages. The `pace` column is the Concept2 split (s/500 m),
from `watts = 2.80 / pace^3` with pace in s/m.

```{r}
rowing <- analyse("rowing")
rowing |>
  filter(method %in% c("Log-log", "ModDmax", "IAT")) |>
  select(method, intensity, pace, lactate)
```

## Swimming: speed in m/s (simulated)

A 7 x 200 m step test, +0.05 m/s per step. Speeds are shown to 0.01 m/s, and the pace per 100 m.

```{r}
swimming <- analyse("swimming")
swimming |>
  filter(method %in% c("Log-log", "ModDmax", "IAT")) |>
  select(method, intensity, pace, heart_rate, rpe)
autoplot(swimming, "ModDmax")
```

## Cases that need care

### An early lactate dip

Lactate can fall after the first stage, when the warm-up was hard or short. `lactate_checks()` flags it, because
it shapes D<sub>max</sub> and the baseline of Bsln+.

```{r}
dip <- analyse("cycling_early_dip")
lactate_checks(dip)
autoplot(dip, "Dmax")
```

### No resting sample, 5-min steps

The [Heuberger et al. (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0206846) test starts at 175 W with no resting sample. Bsln+ then uses the first stage as its
baseline, and `lactate_checks()` says so.

```{r}
no_rest <- analyse("cycling_5min_no_rest")
lactate_checks(no_rest) |>
  filter(check == "Resting sample")
```

### A submaximal test

The simulated client stopped at about 3 mmol/L, before the second turn point. Fitting two turn points would invent
one; `ltp_breakpoints = 1` fits only LTP1, and `lactate_checks()` suggests it when peak lactate stays low.

```{r}
lactate_checks(analyse("submaximal")) |>
  filter(check %in% c("Thresholds found", "Peak lactate"))

submaximal <- analyse("submaximal", ltp_breakpoints = 1)
submaximal |>
  filter(method %in% c("LTP1", "LTP2", "OBLA 4.0")) |>
  select(method, intensity, lactate)
```

## One athlete over five years

The six `cycling_series` tests come from one rider. See [Comparing tests](compare.html)
for how to tell a real change from noise.

```{r}
lactate_tests |>
  filter(athlete == "cyclist_series") |>
  lactate_threshold(intensity, lactate, method = "LTP", plot = FALSE, .by = "day") |>
  select(day, method, intensity, lactate)
```
